# Getting Started with Muse Skills

Curated by Skill Harbor: this is the onboarding guide of the awesome-muse-skills repo itself, the skill to read first. It explains plainly what a skill is: a portable, reusable playbook, a short markdown file called SKILL.md with a small frontmatter header (name, description, category) and a five-section body (Overview, When to use, Core concepts, Practical workflow, Common pitfalls). Its honest headline, as of 2026-09-26: there is no official documented flow to install a SKILL.md in Meta's personal Muse assistant, no verified settings page, upload button, or plugin store, so the practical path today is low-tech: copy the SKILL.md text, paste it into chat, and ask Muse to use it or remember it for relevant tasks. It also teaches the anatomy of a good skill, safety norms (a skill never needs your credentials, never paste secrets), how to write your own in 80 to 150 lines, and how to contribute back to the repo with a pull request. By @aicodedecode, listed here with credit to its creator. Discovered via awesome-muse-skills. Honest caveats: this is the repo's own onboarding guide from a small, recent, unofficial community catalog; the content is generic and works with any AI assistant, not specifically Muse despite the repo name; and there is no install button today, so if nothing seems to happen, you probably never pasted the skill into the chat. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
